days.title: Summit Peaks and Northern Slopes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Hvannadalshnúkur
stops.detail: Its highest peak Hvannadalshnúkur is, at 2110 m, the highest elevation in Iceland.

stops.name: Hnappar
stops.detail: The volcano was previously called Hnappafellsjökull, the designation Knappafell is also found for the mountain, while on the other hand, mountain peaks at the summit are called Hnappar and a farm at its foot Hnappavellir.

stops.name: Svínafell

stops.name: Svínafellsjökull
stops.detail: The outlet glaciers include, for example, Svínafellsjökull (in the west) or Kvíajökull (in the south), which has the highest glacier moraines in Iceland at 100 meters.

stops.name: Fjallsjökull

stops.name: Ingólfshöfði
stops.detail: Although the first settler, Ingólfur Arnarson, came ashore nearby at Ingólfshöfði around the year 870 and then settled in Reykjavík, this area itself was not settled until much later.
